about: House recipes, batch 04 (slice C): written by Claude in a Max-plan session, original, ai-draft. Nutrition is a per-serve estimate kept as data only.

recipes.title: Bouillabaisse-Style Fish Soup with Rouille
recipes.summary: A saffron and fennel-seed fish soup with mussels and prawns, served with garlicky rouille on toasted baguette.
steps: Soften the onion and leek in the oil for 8 minutes until translucent, then add the garlic and fennel seeds and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in the tomato paste, tomatoes, saffron and fish stock and simmer for 25 minutes until the broth is rich and slightly reduced.
Whisk the mayonnaise with the paprika, grated garlic and a spoonful of the hot broth to make the rouille.
Add the fish and mussels to the pot, cover and cook for 5 minutes until the fish turns opaque and the mussel shells have opened.
Add the prawns for 2 minutes until pink and opaque, then discard any mussels that stay shut.
Toast the baguette until crisp, ladle the soup into bowls and serve with the rouille on the toast.
notes: Food safety: cook the fish until opaque and flaking, and the prawns until pink and opaque. Discard any mussel that does not open.
Rouille uses shop-bought mayonnaise so there is no raw egg to worry about.

recipes.title: Beef Pho from Scratch
recipes.summary: A clear spiced beef broth simmered for hours, poured over rice noodles, brisket, sprouts and fresh herbs.
steps: Cover the bones with cold water in a large pot, boil for 10 minutes, then drain and rinse the bones and pot to keep the broth clear.
Char the onions and ginger in a dry pan over high heat for 6 minutes until blackened in spots.
Return the bones to the pot with the brisket, charred aromatics, spices, rock sugar and 3 litres of fresh water, then bring to a bare simmer.
Simmer gently for 3 hours, skimming off the scum, until the brisket is tender when pierced with a knife.
Lift out the brisket, cool a little and slice thinly against the grain, then strain the broth and season with the fish sauce.
Soak the noodles in hot water until soft, then divide among bowls with the brisket.
Ladle over the boiling broth and top with sprouts, herbs, chilli and lime wedges.
notes: Food safety: simmer the brisket until tender, with an internal temperature of at least 75°C.
Keep the broth just below a boil for a clear result.

recipes.title: Chicken Consomme with Herb Royale
recipes.summary: A crystal-clear chicken consomme clarified with an egg-white raft, served with delicate herb custard cubes.
steps: Heat the oven to 160°C and whisk the egg yolks with the milk, chives, nutmeg and half the salt, then pour into a small greased dish.
Bake the custard in a tray of hot water for 20 minutes until just set in the centre, then cool and cut into small cubes.
Mix the mince, egg whites, vegetables and tomato in a cold pot, then stir in the cold stock and bay leaf.
Heat gently, stirring now and then, until a raft forms on the surface at about 80°C, then stop stirring.
Simmer very gently for 45 minutes, making a small hole in the raft so the liquid bubbles through.
Ladle the clear broth through a muslin-lined sieve without disturbing the raft, and season with the remaining salt.
Warm the consomme, drop a few custard cubes into each bowl and serve hot.
notes: Food safety: the mince cooks in the raft; the consomme should simmer for the full 45 minutes so the chicken reaches at least 75°C. Cook the custard until set.
Strain gently for the clearest result.

recipes.title: Fermented Flatbread, Injera-Style
recipes.summary: A soft, tangy, spongy pancake fermented for two days, for scooping up stews and salads.
steps: Whisk the flours, yeast and 500ml of the water into a smooth batter, cover loosely and leave at room temperature for two days until bubbly and sour.
Stir the batter, add the salt and enough of the remaining water to make a thin pouring consistency like cream.
Heat a non-stick pan over medium heat and wipe with the oil on a paper towel.
Pour in a thin layer, swirling to cover the base, and cover with a lid for 2 minutes until the surface is full of holes and set.
Slide it out without flipping and cool on a clean cloth, cooking the remaining batter in the same way until all the pancakes are done.
Stack once cool and serve with stews, lentils and salads.
notes: Traditionally made with teff flour; this is a simple everyday version.
Fermenting time is not counted in the prep time.

recipes.title: Mtori Tanzanian Beef and Plantain Soup
recipes.summary: A creamy beef and plantain soup from Tanzania, thickened with the cooked plantain and finished with a little cream.
steps: Brown the beef in the oil for 5 minutes until coloured on all sides, then lift it out.
Cook the onion and garlic in the same pot for 5 minutes until soft, then add the tomatoes until they break down.
Return the beef with the water and salt, bring to the boil, then simmer for 40 minutes until the beef is tender.
Add the plantains and simmer for 15 minutes until completely soft.
Lift out a few pieces of beef, blend the soup until smooth and return the beef to the pot with the cream.
Heat through, season with the pepper and serve with the coriander.
notes: Food safety: simmer the beef until tender, with an internal temperature of at least 75°C before serving.
Choose green or very firm plantains for the traditional texture.

recipes.title: Sukuma Wiki with Tomato and Onion
recipes.summary: Kenyan braised greens with soft onion and tomato, the everyday side served with ugali.
steps: Fry the onion in the oil for 6 minutes until golden and soft, then add the garlic and coriander and cook for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 4 minutes until pulpy.
Stir in the kale, water and salt, cover and cook for 6 minutes until the greens are tender but still bright.
Taste and adjust the salt before serving hot.
notes: Add a chopped chilli if you like heat.
Leftovers keep for 3 days in the fridge.

recipes.title: Ugali with Kachumbari Salad
recipes.summary: Stiff maize porridge to scoop with the fresh tomato, onion and chilli salad of Kenya and Tanzania.
steps: Bring the water and salt to the boil in a heavy pot, then whisk in a third of the polenta until smooth.
Add the rest gradually, beating with a wooden spoon, and cook on low heat for 12 minutes until the mass pulls away from the pot.
Mix the tomatoes, onion, chilli, coriander and lime juice in a bowl.
Shape the ugali into mounds with a wet spoon and serve with the kachumbari.
notes: Eat with your hands: pinch off a piece of ugali and use it to scoop up the salad.
Rest the salad for 10 minutes for the best flavour.

recipes.title: Maharagwe ya Nazi Coconut Beans
recipes.summary: Swahili-coast kidney beans simmered in coconut milk with tomato, garlic and turmeric.
steps: Cook the onion in the oil for 6 minutes until soft, then add the garlic, turmeric and cumin for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes until jammy.
Stir in the beans and coconut milk and simmer for 12 minutes until thick and creamy.
Season with salt and scatter over the coriander.
notes: Serve with rice, chapati or ugali.
Mash a few beans against the pot to thicken it.

recipes.title: Mukimo Mashed Potato with Peas and Corn
recipes.summary: Kikuyu-style mash of potatoes, green peas and sweetcorn, a comforting side for stews.
steps: Boil the potatoes in salted water for 15 minutes until a knife slides in easily.
Add the peas and corn for the last 4 minutes of cooking, then drain.
Fry the onion in the butter for 5 minutes until soft and golden.
Mash everything with the milk and onion until chunky and green-flecked.
Serve hot with a stew or grilled meat.
notes: Leave some lumps for the traditional texture.
Use oat milk and oil for a dairy-free version.

recipes.title: Pili Pili Hot Sauce
recipes.summary: A bright East African chilli, garlic and lime sauce that keeps well in the fridge.
steps: Simmer the chillies, garlic and water for 5 minutes until the chillies are soft.
Blend with the lime juice, oil, salt and paprika until smooth.
Cool completely and store in a clean jar.
Serve with grilled meats, eggs or beans.
notes: Keeps for 2 weeks in the fridge.
Wear gloves when chopping the chillies.

recipes.title: Jamaican Chicken Soup with Pumpkin and Dumplings
recipes.summary: A turmeric-gold chicken and root vegetable soup with chewy spinner dumplings and a little scotch bonnet heat.
steps: Simmer the chicken in the stock with the thyme, allspice, turmeric and whole scotch bonnet for 30 minutes until the meat is tender.
Lift out the chicken, shred the meat and discard the skin and bones.
Add the pumpkin and carrot to the broth and simmer for 12 minutes until soft.
Mix the flour, water and salt into a firm dough and roll small pieces into thin spinners between your palms.
Drop the spinners into the soup and cook for 8 minutes until firm and cooked through.
Return the chicken and add the spring onions, then remove the scotch bonnet before serving.
notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until it reaches an internal temperature of 75°C and the juices run clear.
Leave the scotch bonnet whole for flavour without the full heat.

recipes.title: Callaloo and Crab Soup
recipes.summary: A green Trinidadian soup of spinach, okra and coconut milk with sweet crab meat.
steps: Melt the butter and cook the onion and garlic for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the okra, thyme, whole scotch bonnet and stock and simmer for 10 minutes until the okra is tender.
Add the spinach until wilted, then blend the soup until smooth, keeping the scotch bonnet out.
Stir in the coconut milk and simmer for 8 minutes.
Fold in the crab and heat gently for 3 minutes until hot and opaque, then season with salt.
notes: Food safety: heat the crab until opaque and piping hot.
Remove the scotch bonnet before blending.

recipes.title: Haitian Pikliz Pickled Slaw
recipes.summary: A fiery crunchy cabbage and carrot pickle that cuts the richness of fried foods.
steps: Pack the cabbage, carrot, capsicum, scotch bonnet and spring onions into a clean jar with the cloves.
Pour over the vinegar, lime juice and salt, adding water to cover if needed.
Press down until the vegetables are submerged and seal.
Chill for at least 24 hours before serving.
notes: Keeps for 3 weeks in the fridge.
Wear gloves to slice the scotch bonnet.

recipes.title: Rice and Peas with Coconut and Thyme
recipes.summary: Jamaican Sunday side of rice cooked in coconut milk with kidney beans, thyme and allspice.
steps: Rinse the rice until the water runs clear.
Bring the coconut milk, water, beans, thyme, spring onions, allspice, garlic and whole scotch bonnet to a simmer until steaming, seasoning with the salt.
Stir in the rice, cover and cook on the lowest heat for 20 minutes until the liquid is absorbed and the rice is tender.
Rest for 10 minutes covered, then remove the thyme and scotch bonnet and fluff with a fork.
notes: Food safety: cool leftover rice quickly and refrigerate within an hour, and reheat until steaming hot.
Keep the scotch bonnet whole to avoid blowing your head off.

recipes.title: Fried Sweet Plantain
recipes.summary: Ripe plantain slices fried until caramelised and golden, a staple side across the Caribbean.

items: 3 plantains, peeled and sliced on an angle

steps: Heat half the oil in a wide pan over medium heat.
Fry the plantain in batches for 3 minutes each side until deep golden with dark edges.
Drain on paper towel and sprinkle with salt.
Serve warm with lime wedges.
notes: Use very ripe plantains with black skins for the sweetest result.
Add the rest of the oil as you go.

recipes.title: Johnny Cakes with Scrambled Eggs and Tomato
recipes.summary: Golden fried cornmeal-flour dumplings from the islands, served with soft scrambled eggs and tomato.
steps: Rub the butter into the flour, baking powder, sugar and salt until crumbly.
Stir in the water to make a soft dough, divide into 8 pieces and flatten into discs.
Fry the discs in 2 tbsp oil for 3 minutes each side until golden and cooked in the middle.
Heat the remaining oil in another pan, add the tomatoes and spring onions for 2 minutes.
Pour in the whisked eggs and stir gently over low heat for 3 minutes until set and no liquid egg remains.
Serve the eggs with the warm johnny cakes.
notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until firm with no runny egg, and serve immediately.
Johnny cakes freeze well.

recipes.title: Jerk Marinade
recipes.summary: A sweet-hot paste of scotch bonnet, allspice and thyme for chicken, pork, fish or vegetables.
steps: Blitz the scotch bonnets, spring onions, garlic and ginger until a rough paste forms.
Add the allspice, thyme, soy sauce, lime juice, sugar, oil and pepper and blitz until nearly smooth.
Rub over your protein and marinate for at least 4 hours before cooking.
Store leftover marinade in a jar for up to 2 weeks.
notes: Food safety: cook marinated chicken to 75°C and pork to at least 70°C, and never reuse marinade that touched raw meat.
Works beautifully with tofu or cauliflower too.

recipes.title: Mango and Scotch Bonnet Hot Sauce
recipes.summary: A sweet, tangy and fiery Caribbean table sauce to dollop on grilled fish, rice and eggs.
steps: Simmer the mango, scotch bonnet, garlic, vinegar and turmeric for 12 minutes until the mango is very soft.
Blend with the lime juice, honey and salt until completely smooth.
Cool and bottle in a clean jar.
Keep in the fridge for up to 3 weeks.
notes: Use a whole scotch bonnet for more heat.
Shake before using.

recipes.title: Cornmeal Porridge with Coconut and Nutmeg
recipes.summary: Creamy Jamaican cornmeal porridge sweetened with condensed-style sugar, coconut milk and warming spice.
steps: Whisk the polenta with 250ml of the water until smooth.
Bring the remaining water, coconut milk, cinnamon, nutmeg and salt to a simmer until steaming.
Stir in the polenta mixture and cook over low heat for 15 minutes until thick and creamy.
Add the sugar and vanilla and stir until dissolved.
notes: Loosen with a splash of milk if it thickens as it cools.
Naturally dairy-free and gluten-free.

recipes.title: Soto Ayam Indonesian Chicken Soup
recipes.summary: A turmeric-gold chicken broth with lemongrass and galangal, vermicelli, egg and fresh sprouts.
steps: Blitz the garlic, shallots, turmeric and coriander with a splash of water to a paste and fry in the oil for 4 minutes until fragrant.
Add the chicken, water, lemongrass, lime leaves, galangal and salt and simmer for 35 minutes until the chicken is cooked through.
Boil the eggs for 8 minutes until firm, then peel and halve.
Lift out the chicken, shred it and soak the vermicelli in hot water until soft.
Strain the broth and divide the noodles, chicken, eggs and sprouts among bowls.
Ladle over the hot broth and top with spring onion and lime.
notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until it reaches 75°C and boil the eggs until the whites and yolks are firm.
Serve with sambal on the side.

recipes.title: Gado-Gado Vegetable Platter with Tofu
recipes.summary: Blanched vegetables, tofu and eggs under a warm sweet-spicy peanut dressing.
steps: Boil the potatoes for 12 minutes until tender, then lift out and cool.
Blanch the beans, cabbage and sprouts in the same water for 2 minutes until just tender, then refresh in cold water.
Boil the eggs for 9 minutes until the yolks are firm, then cool, peel and quarter.
Warm the peanut butter, water, kecap manis, lime juice, garlic and chilli in a pot until smooth and pourable.
Arrange the vegetables, tofu, cucumber and eggs on a platter.
Spoon over the sauce and finish with the fried shallots.
notes: Food safety: boil the eggs until the yolks are firm.
Swap the eggs for extra tofu to make it vegan.

recipes.title: Sambal Matah Lemongrass and Shallot Sambal
recipes.summary: A raw Balinese relish of shallots, lemongrass, chilli and lime, warmed with a splash of hot oil.
steps: Toast the shrimp paste in a dry pan for 1 minute until fragrant.
Mix the shallots, lemongrass, chillies and lime leaves in a bowl.
Heat the coconut oil until shimmering and pour over the mixture.
Stir in the lime juice, shrimp paste and salt and rest for 10 minutes before serving.
notes: Serve with grilled fish, chicken or rice.
Best eaten the day it is made.

recipes.title: Bubur Ayam Indonesian Chicken Rice Porridge
recipes.summary: A silky rice porridge with shredded chicken, fried shallots, spring onion and a soy egg.
steps: Simmer the rice with the stock, garlic and ginger, stirring occasionally, for 45 minutes until the grains collapse into a thick porridge.
Poach the chicken in the porridge for 15 minutes until cooked through, then lift out and shred.
Boil the eggs for 7 minutes until jammy, then peel and halve.
Season the porridge with salt and spoon into bowls.
Top with chicken, egg, kecap manis, spring onion and fried shallots.
notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until it reaches 75°C and the juices run clear.
Add water if the porridge gets too thick.

recipes.title: Sayur Lodeh Vegetable Coconut Soup
recipes.summary: A gentle Javanese soup of mixed vegetables in lemongrass-scented turmeric coconut broth.
steps: Blitz the shallots, garlic, turmeric and coriander with a splash of water to a paste.
Fry the paste in the oil for 4 minutes until fragrant.
Add the stock, coconut milk, lemongrass and pumpkin and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the carrot, beans and cabbage and simmer for 8 minutes until the vegetables are tender.
Season with salt and remove the lemongrass before serving.
notes: Serve with rice.
Add tofu or tempeh-style firm tofu for protein.

recipes.title: Bakso Indonesian Meatball Soup
recipes.summary: Springy beef meatballs in a peppery garlic broth with noodles and greens.
steps: Blitz the mince, tapioca starch, 2 garlic cloves, salt, pepper and egg to a sticky paste.
Bring the stock to a gentle simmer with the remaining garlic until steaming.
Roll the mixture into walnut-sized balls and drop into the stock.
Simmer for 15 minutes until the balls float and are cooked through.
Add the bok choy for 2 minutes until just tender and soak the vermicelli in hot water until soft.
Divide the noodles among bowls, ladle over the meatballs and broth, then top with shallots, spring onion and kecap manis.
notes: Food safety: cook the meatballs until they reach an internal temperature of 75°C and no pink remains.
Serve with sambal.

recipes.title: Acar Timun Pickled Cucumber Salad
recipes.summary: A sweet-sour cucumber, carrot and shallot pickle served alongside satay and fried rice.
steps: Heat the vinegar, sugar, water and salt until the sugar has dissolved, then cool.
Combine the cucumber, carrot, shallots and chillies in a bowl.
Pour over the cooled pickling liquid and stir.
Chill for 30 minutes, then top with the peanuts.
notes: Keeps for 3 days in the fridge.
Peanuts are optional.

recipes.title: Nasi Uduk Coconut Rice
recipes.summary: Jakarta-style fragrant rice cooked in coconut milk with lemongrass, bay leaf and pandan-style lime leaves.
steps: Rinse the rice until the water runs clear.
Combine the rice, coconut milk, water, lemongrass, bay leaves, lime leaves and salt in a pot.
Bring to a simmer, cover and cook on the lowest heat for 18 minutes until the rice is tender and the liquid absorbed.
Rest for 10 minutes covered and fluff, removing the aromatics, then top with fried shallots.
notes: Food safety: refrigerate any leftover rice within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Serve with fried tofu and sambal.

recipes.title: Arroz Caldo Filipino Chicken and Ginger Rice Porridge
recipes.summary: A warming ginger and garlic rice porridge with chicken, boiled egg and crisp garlic.
steps: Fry the onion, ginger and half the garlic in the oil for 5 minutes until soft and golden.
Add the chicken, rice and stock and simmer for 40 minutes, stirring now and then, until the rice breaks down and the chicken is tender.
Lift out the chicken, shred the meat, discard the bones and skin, and stir the meat back through with the fish sauce.
Boil the eggs for 8 minutes until firm, then peel and halve.
Fry the remaining garlic in a little oil for 2 minutes until golden and crisp.
Top bowls with egg, crisp garlic, spring onion and a squeeze of lemon.
notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until it reaches 75°C and boil the eggs until the yolks are firm.
Add more stock for a looser porridge.

recipes.title: Sinigang na Hipon Sour Tamarind Prawn Soup
recipes.summary: The classic Filipino sour soup of tamarind, tomato and prawns with greens.
steps: Simmer the water, tamarind, tomatoes and onion for 10 minutes until the tomatoes soften.
Add the daikon and cook for 8 minutes until tender.
Add the green beans and chillies and simmer for 4 minutes.
Stir in the prawns for 3 minutes until pink and opaque.
Fold through the spinach until just wilted and season with the fish sauce.
notes: Food safety: cook the prawns until pink and opaque.
Adjust the tamarind to taste for more sourness.

recipes.title: Tinolang Manok Chicken, Ginger and Green Papaya Soup
recipes.summary: A clear, comforting Filipino soup of chicken, plenty of ginger and green papaya.
steps: Fry the ginger, onion and garlic in the oil for 4 minutes until fragrant.
Add the chicken and brown for 5 minutes.
Pour in the water and fish sauce, bring to the boil and simmer for 20 minutes until the chicken is tender.
Add the green papaya and cook for 8 minutes until just tender.
Stir in the spinach and chilli until wilted.
notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until it reaches 75°C and the juices run clear.
Use chayote or zucchini if papaya is hard to find.

recipes.title: Bulalo Filipino Beef Shank Soup
recipes.summary: A long-simmered beef shank soup with sweet corn, cabbage and bok choy in a clear, rich broth.
steps: Boil the beef shin in water for 10 minutes, then drain, rinse and wipe out the pot to keep the broth clear.
Return the beef to the pot with the water, onion and peppercorns and bring to a bare simmer until the surface just trembles.
Simmer for 2.5 hours, skimming off scum, until the meat is falling off the bone.
Add the fish sauce, corn and potatoes and cook for 20 minutes until the potatoes are tender.
Add the cabbage and bok choy and cook for 4 minutes until just soft.
Season with salt and serve with rice.
notes: Food safety: simmer the beef until tender, with an internal temperature of at least 75°C.
Skim the fat for a lighter broth.

recipes.title: Ensaladang Mangga Green Mango Salad
recipes.summary: Crunchy green mango with tomato, red onion and a salty-sweet dressing.
steps: Mix the mangoes, tomatoes and onion in a bowl.
Whisk the fish sauce, lime juice and sugar until the sugar dissolves.
Toss through the salad until coated.
Top with chilli and coriander and serve.
notes: Use firm, unripe mango for the right crunch.
Serve with grilled fish or pork.

recipes.title: Ensaladang Talong Charred Eggplant Salad
recipes.summary: Smoky grilled eggplant with tomato, onion and a sharp vinegar dressing.
steps: Char the whole eggplants over a flame or under a hot grill for 15 minutes, turning often, until the skin is blackened and the flesh collapses.
Cool, peel and chop the flesh.
Whisk the vinegar, fish sauce, garlic and sugar in a bowl.
Toss with the eggplant, tomato, onion and chilli and serve.
notes: Serve with fried fish or rice.
Leave out the fish sauce and use soy for a vegetarian version.

recipes.title: Tortang Talong Eggplant Omelette
recipes.summary: A silky charred eggplant folded into an egg omelette, served with ketchup or vinegar.
steps: Char the whole eggplants under a hot grill for 12 minutes until blackened and soft.
Cool, peel and flatten the flesh with a fork, keeping the stems on.
Whisk the eggs with the salt and spring onion.
Heat the oil in a pan, dip the eggplants in the egg and fry for 3 minutes each side until set and golden.
Serve hot with tomato sauce.
notes: Food safety: cook the omelette until the egg is completely set.
Serve with garlic rice.

recipes.title: Sinangag Filipino Garlic Fried Rice
recipes.summary: The breakfast staple of crisp garlic and day-old rice, served with eggs and cured meats.
steps: Break up the cold rice with your fingers.
Fry the garlic in 1 tbsp oil over medium heat for 2 minutes until golden.
Add the rice and salt and stir-fry for 5 minutes until hot and lightly crisp.
Fry the eggs in the remaining oil until the whites are set.
Serve the rice with the eggs and spring onion on top.
notes: Food safety: cool cooked rice quickly and refrigerate within an hour, and cook the fried rice until steaming hot all through.
Cook the eggs until the whites are fully set.

recipes.title: Atchara Pickled Green Papaya
recipes.summary: A sweet and tangy Filipino pickle of green papaya, carrot and capsicum for fried and grilled food.
steps: Mix the papaya, carrot, capsicum, onion and ginger with the salt and leave for 20 minutes, then squeeze out the liquid.
Heat the vinegar, sugar and pepper until the sugar has dissolved.
Pack the vegetables into clean jars and pour over the warm pickling liquid.
Cool, seal and chill for at least 2 days before serving.
notes: Keeps for a month in the fridge.
Pickling time is not counted.

recipes.title: Sawsawan Spiced Vinegar Dipping Sauce
recipes.summary: A garlicky chilli vinegar dip for fried fish, grilled meat and spring rolls.
steps: Combine all the ingredients in a small bowl.
Stir until the sugar dissolves.
Rest for 15 minutes so the flavours mellow before serving.
notes: Keeps for a week in the fridge.
Add a squeeze of calamansi or lime for extra zing.

recipes.title: Chakalaka South African Vegetable Relish
recipes.summary: A warming braai relish of capsicum, carrot, beans and curry spices.
steps: Fry the onion in the oil for 6 minutes until soft, then add the garlic, ginger, curry powder and paprika for 1 minute.
Stir in the capsicum and carrot and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and chilli and simmer for 10 minutes until thick.
Stir through the beans and heat for 4 minutes, then season with salt.
notes: Serve warm or cold with pap, grilled meat or bread.
Keeps for 5 days in the fridge.

recipes.title: Pap and Tomato Gravy
recipes.summary: Stiff maize porridge with a sweet-sharp tomato and onion gravy, a staple side.
steps: Bring the water and salt to the boil, whisk in the polenta and cook over low heat for 15 minutes, stirring, until thick and stiff.
Fry the onion in the oil for 6 minutes until soft, then add the garlic and curry powder.
Add the tomatoes, sugar and bay leaf and simmer for 12 minutes until saucy.
Shape the pap into mounds and ladle over the gravy.
notes: Serve with grilled sausage or chicken.
Remove the bay leaf before serving.

recipes.title: Cape Malay Butternut Soup
recipes.summary: A silky pumpkin soup spiced with cinnamon, ginger and curry, topped with toasted seeds.
steps: Soften the onion in the butter for 6 minutes until translucent.
Add the garlic, ginger, curry powder and cinnamon for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the pumpkin and stock, cover and simmer for 20 minutes until the pumpkin is completely soft.
Blend until smooth, stir in the cream and heat through.
Serve with toasted pumpkin seeds.
notes: Use coconut cream for a dairy-free version.
Toast the seeds in a dry pan until golden.

recipes.title: Mealie Bread with Cheddar
recipes.summary: A moist sweetcorn loaf studded with cheese, perfect warm with butter or alongside a braai.
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C and grease a loaf tin.
Mix the polenta, flour, baking powder, salt and sugar.
Whisk the eggs, milk and butter, then stir into the dry mix with the corn and cheese.
Pour into the tin and bake for 45 minutes until golden and a skewer comes out clean.
Rest in the tin for 10 minutes before slicing.
notes: Food safety: the egg is cooked once a skewer comes out clean and the centre reaches at least 75°C.
Serve with butter and chakalaka.

recipes.title: South African Peri-Peri Basting Sauce
recipes.summary: A smoky garlic and chilli sauce for basting chicken, prawns or halloumi.
steps: Blitz the chillies, capsicum, garlic, lemon juice, vinegar, paprika and oregano to a chunky sauce.
Heat the oil in a pan and cook the sauce for 8 minutes until darker and thicker.
Season with salt and cool.
Store in a jar in the fridge for up to 2 weeks.
notes: Food safety: use a clean spoon each time, and bring any marinade that touched raw chicken to the boil before using as a sauce, cooking the chicken to 75°C.
Swap in dried chilli for more smoke.

recipes.title: Savoury Vetkoek Buns Filled with Spiced Beef
recipes.summary: Crisp, airy fried bread buns split and filled with fragrant curried beef mince.
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and salt, add the warm water and knead for 5 minutes until the dough is soft, then rise for 1 hour until doubled.
Fry the onion in a little oil for 5 minutes until soft, add the mince and garlic and brown for 6 minutes.
Stir in the curry powder, tomatoes and chutney and simmer for 15 minutes until thick.
Heat the oil to 170°C and fry golf-ball sized pieces of dough for 5 minutes, turning, until deep golden and cooked in the middle.
Split the vetkoek and spoon in the mince.
notes: Food safety: cook the mince until it reaches 75°C with no pink remaining.
Resting time is not counted in the prep time.

recipes.title: Pampoenkoekies Pumpkin Fritters
recipes.summary: Cinnamon-sugar pumpkin fritters, a traditional South African side with roasts.
steps: Mix the pumpkin, flour, baking powder, egg, 1 tbsp sugar and salt into a thick batter.
Heat the oil in a pan over medium heat.
Spoon in tablespoons of batter and fry for 3 minutes each side until golden and cooked in the middle.
Drain and roll in the remaining sugar mixed with the cinnamon.
notes: Food safety: cook the fritters until golden and set in the middle.
Roast the pumpkin first for the best flavour.

recipes.title: Palusami Spinach in Coconut Cream
recipes.summary: Samoan-style parcels of greens baked in coconut cream with onion, a luscious side for roasts.
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C and lightly grease a baking dish.
Mix the coconut cream with the onion, salt and lemon juice.
Layer the spinach in a baking dish and pour over the coconut mixture.
Cover with foil and bake for 25 minutes until the greens are soft and the cream has thickened.
Stir well until creamy and serve hot alongside roast meat or fish.
notes: Traditionally made with taro leaves.
Serve with roast pork, fish or sweet potato.

recipes.title: Hawaiian-Style Macaroni Salad
recipes.summary: A creamy plate-lunch macaroni salad with carrot, onion and a touch of sweetness.
steps: Cook the macaroni until completely soft, a minute longer than the packet, then drain and rinse.
Whisk the mayonnaise, vinegar, sugar, salt and pepper in a bowl.
Fold through the warm macaroni, carrot, onion and celery.
Chill for at least 1 hour before serving.
notes: Serve with rice and grilled meat as a plate lunch.
The pasta absorbs the dressing, so loosen with milk if needed.

recipes.title: Lomi Lomi Smoked Salmon Salad
recipes.summary: Hawaiian-style salad of salmon, tomato and sweet onion, fresh and bright with lime.
steps: Mix the salmon, tomatoes, onion and spring onions in a bowl.
Add the lime juice, oil, salt and chilli flakes and toss gently.
Chill until cold, about 15 minutes, so the flavours mingle.
Serve in small bowls with rice or crackers.
notes: Use fresh sashimi-grade salmon only if you are confident of its source; smoked salmon is the safer option.
Serve with rice or crackers.

recipes.title: Kumara Hash with Fried Egg and Spring Onion
recipes.summary: Crisp pan-fried sweet potato hash topped with a runny-yolk egg.
steps: Toss the sweet potato with the salt and paprika.
Fry in the coconut oil in a wide pan over medium heat for 12 minutes, turning, until crisp and golden.
Make two wells and crack in the eggs, cover and cook for 4 minutes until the whites are set.
Scatter with spring onion and coriander.
notes: Food safety: cook the egg whites until completely set; cook the yolk through for children, pregnant women and the elderly.
Add chilli for kick.

recipes.title: Fijian Fish and Coconut Soup
recipes.summary: A light, lime-bright broth of coconut milk, fresh fish and tomatoes.
steps: Cook the onion, garlic and ginger in a little coconut milk for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the tomatoes, stock and remaining coconut milk and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the fish and chilli and simmer gently for 5 minutes until the fish is opaque and flakes easily.
Finish with the lime juice, salt and coriander.
notes: Food safety: cook the fish until opaque and flaking, with an internal temperature of at least 63°C.
Do not boil hard or the fish will break up.
